title: Mind What You Ask For: Emotional and Rational Faces of Persuasion by Large Language Models

live_model.evidence: "OpenAI [OpenAI, 2024]: GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4, GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-4o" (Sec. 2, one of 12 tested models); grouped among models with "highest baseline scores" for the all-or-none LIWC category

prompt.location: Table 1 (Baseline/Emotional/Rational prompt templates printed in full)
prompt.note: Baseline prompt administered 60 times per model via LangChain.

claim.metric: LIWC 'all-or-none' thinking-style category (% of words), emotional-setup responses
claim.location: Sec. 4.1 groups GPT-4 Turbo among models with the "highest baseline scores" in this category, but only cites exact figures for GPT-3.5 Turbo (1.04) and GPT-4 (1.2), not GPT-4 Turbo specifically

data.source: Persuasion-task prompt dataset (Mieleszczenko-Kowszewicz et al. 2024) plus the paper's own baseline generations; LIWC-22 is a licensed (not free) analysis tool

notes: Methodology is clean and fully reproducible (full prompt templates, n=60/model for the baseline condition, mechanical LIWC scoring so no LLM judge needed). Soft gap: the extracted text states GPT-4 Turbo's category membership (among the highest scorers) but does not give its exact numeric value, only examples for two other models in the same group.
